html:
Atropatene was an ancient Iranian kingdom in what is now northwestern Iran, founded around 323 BCE by the Persian governor Atropates. It is shown here in 323 and 300 BCE.

Atropates had commanded troops for the Achaemenid king at the Battle of Gaugamela. He then went over to Alexander the Great, who left him as governor of northern Media. When Alexander died, Atropates kept his province as a kingdom of his own, and it stayed out of the Seleucid Empire's direct rule.

His descendants ruled until the early 1st century CE, between the Seleucids, Armenia, Rome and the Parthian Empire. In 36 BCE Mark Antony besieged its capital, Phraaspa, and failed. Later Parthian princes ruled it, and the Sasanians absorbed it in the 220s CE. The region was a Zoroastrian heartland. Its name lives on in "Azerbaijan", from the Middle Persian Adurbadagan.
